metadata.name: regime_oracle
metadata.description: Vigil regime-aware pricing oracle: anchor-decay-clamp blend between Pyth and a keeper-posted DEX reference

instructions.name: initialize
docs: One-time setup of a `RegimeState` PDA for a given Pyth price feed id
(one per collateral asset, matching the isolated-market design).

accounts.name: keeper_authority
docs: The keeper authority permitted to call `set_regime` and
`post_dex_reference` for this market. Set once at init; there is no
admin instruction to change it (out of scope per the MVP brief --
redeploy with a new keeper if it needs to rotate).

instructions.name: post_dex_reference
docs: Keeper-only: records the latest off-chain-computed DEX TWAP and the
liquidity depth it was computed over.

accounts.name: keeper_authority
docs: Must match `regime_state.keeper_authority`. Permissioned: the DEX
reference is only as trustworthy as whoever is allowed to post it.

instructions.name: set_regime
docs: Keeper-only: flips the market open/closed flag.

accounts.name: keeper_authority
docs: Must match `regime_state.keeper_authority`. Permissioned so no
arbitrary signer can flip a market's open/closed flag.

instructions.name: update_price
docs: Permissionless crank: recomputes Borrow-Limit Price and Liquidation
Price via the anchor-decay-clamp blend.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Permissionless: anyone may crank a recompute. Every input this
instruction trusts (the Pyth update, the keeper-posted DEX
reference, the regime flag) is independently authenticated --
Pyth's own signature/verification, or a prior keeper-only
instruction -- so the caller here doesn't need to be privileged.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: Required and read only while the market is open; ignored while
closed (during closure Vigil deliberately does NOT trust Pyth's
frozen weekend print -- that's the entire point of the regime
module). Pass any account while closed; it will simply be skipped.
Deliberately `UncheckedAccount`, not `Account<'info, PriceUpdateV2>`:
see the `PYTH_RECEIVER_PROGRAM_ID` doc comment above. Ownership and
deserialization are both checked explicitly in the handler instead.

errors.name: StalePythPrice
errors.msg: Pyth price update is stale beyond the allowed threshold

errors.name: WrongPriceFeed
errors.msg: Pyth price feed id does not match the configured AAPLx feed

errors.name: InvalidPythPrice
errors.msg: Pyth price or confidence is not positive

errors.name: InvalidDexReference
errors.msg: DEX reference price or liquidity is not positive

errors.name: UnauthorizedKeeper
errors.msg: Only the configured keeper authority may call this instruction

errors.name: RegimeUnchanged
errors.msg: Regime is already set to the requested value

errors.name: MissingDexReference
errors.msg: DEX reference has not been posted yet

errors.name: Overflow
errors.msg: Checked arithmetic overflow or underflow in oracle math

errors.name: NonPositivePrice
errors.msg: Price input must be greater than zero

fields.name: keeper_authority
docs: Keeper authority allowed to call `set_regime` and `post_dex_reference`.

fields.name: pyth_receiver_program
docs: The program that must own the account passed as `update_price`'s
`price_update`. Set once at `initialize` (production: Pyth's real
Solana Receiver program, same address on every cluster; local/devnet
testing: a lightweight mock price-setter program, so tests can
exercise the open-market path deterministically without depending
on Hermes). The staleness bound and feed-id check inside
`update_price` are identical either way -- only the trusted account
origin differs, the same kind of documented substitution as the
devnet mock-USDC mint.

fields.name: price_feed_id
docs: The Pyth `PriceUpdateV2` feed id this instance tracks (e.g. AAPLx/USD).

fields.name: is_open
docs: True while the underlying market (NYSE hours) is open.

fields.name: last_regime_change_ts
docs: Unix timestamp of the most recent `is_open` transition.

fields.name: pending_reopen_snap
docs: True only for the single tick immediately following a Closed->Open
transition, so `update_price` knows to apply the wider reopen clamp
instead of the normal per-tick clamp.

fields.name: anchor_price
docs: Last live Pyth price observed while the market was open -- the
"anchor" the decay function blends away from during closure.

fields.name: anchor_ts
docs: Unix timestamp `anchor_price` was captured at.

fields.name: dex_reference_price
docs: Most recent keeper-posted DEX TWAP reference price (micro-USD).

fields.name: dex_reference_liquidity
docs: Most recent keeper-posted DEX pool liquidity depth (micro-USD),
used to dampen the DEX reference's influence on the closed blend.

fields.name: dex_reference_ts
docs: Unix timestamp the DEX reference was last posted.

fields.name: borrow_limit_price
docs: Slow-smoothed, conservative price the lending market uses to compute
borrow limits.

fields.name: liquidation_price
docs: Fast-smoothed, wider-banded price the lending market uses to check
liquidation eligibility.

fields.name: last_update_ts
docs: Unix timestamp the two output prices were last updated.
